features.optics-sfp-plus: product page: "(2) 10 Gb capable SFP+ sockets"; the page names no optic and none is included
features.serial-modes: RS-232 (A models); RS-232, RS-422 and RS-485 software selectable (C models, MEI)

power.power-input: AC, single or dual, C13 connector: 100 - 240 VAC, 50 - 60 Hz, 2.4 A max for each supply (A100, A200, C100, C200). Dual DC with supplied Phoenix connectors: 48 VDC, 2.9 A max for each supply (AD00, CD00)

dual-ac.description: Two AC supplies; RS-232 on the A200 and RS-232/422/485 on the C200.

dual-dc.description: Two DC supplies with Phoenix connectors; RS-232 on the AD00 and RS-232/422/485 on the CD00.

single-ac.description: One AC supply in the first bay and a cover over the second, the CORE socket covered. This is the build the rear photograph shows apart from the modem. RS-232 on the A100 and RS-232/422/485 on the C100.

with-lte-modem.description: The single AC build with a Digi CORE plug-in LTE modem (1002-CMG4-GLB, an accessory) in the CORE socket, as the rear photograph shows it.

description: Digi Connect EZ 32 is a 1U rack-mount serial server (console server) with thirty-two RJ45 10-pin serial ports and a console jack. It also has two 10/100/1000 Ethernet ports, two SFP+ cages and two USB 3.1 Gen 1 Type A ports. There is a micro-SD socket and a socket for a Digi CORE plug-in LTE modem. The front carries the console jack, the USB ports and the SFP+ and Ethernet jacks stacked in pairs. It also has the thirty-two serial jacks in two rows of four blocks of four and a lamp cluster. The rear carries two field-replaceable power supply bays, a system fan, the CORE module bay with its two SMA antenna jacks and an earth stud. The EZ32-A100-GLB and -C100-GLB carry one AC supply, the -A200-GLB and -C200-GLB two, and the -AD00 and -CD00 two DC supplies. The C models add software-selectable RS-232/422/485 to the RS-232 of the A models. It ships with attachable 19-inch rack ears.

gaps.note: No photograph or drawing of the DC supply is held. The EZ32-AD00 and -CD00 builds seat the library part ez-psu-dc, the AC supply's face with a two-position pluggable terminal header where the inlet is. The page says only "Phoenix connectors", and nothing about their positions, pitch, polarity or direction.
gaps.wanted: A photograph or drawing of the Connect EZ DC power supply.

gaps.note: The rear photograph shows one AC supply fitted, the second bay covered and the CORE module fitted. A dual AC rear and a rear with the CORE socket covered are not pictured. The cover over an empty CORE socket is drawn as the module's plate without its jacks.
gaps.wanted: Photographs of the dual AC build and of a unit without the CORE modem.

gaps.note: The photographs are 800 px wide. Small marks beside the USB ports and the SFP+ cages (a trident symbol above each USB, a number beside each), the symbol under the warning triangle on the rear, the PSU1 and PSU2 legends with their rotated "Caution Shock hazard" labels, the model legend under the micro-SD socket and the rating legend printed by the AC inlet do not resolve. The legends that do are drawn; the rest are not.
gaps.wanted: A higher resolution photograph of each face, or Digi's hardware guide.

gaps.note: The page lists no rail or mounting kit for the unit and says only that it ships with attachable 19-inch rack ears, so none is listed.
Digi states each supply's input (2.4 A at 100 - 240 VAC, 2.9 A at 48 VDC) and no power consumed by the unit, the supplies, the fan or the CORE modem, so none is stated.
The page gives a package weight (5.26 kg for the EZ 32) and no weight for the unit.
The page names the lamps and no colour or state of any of them. The Ethernet and serial jacks' lamps' colours do not resolve in the 800 px photographs.
The USB ports are drawn without a number because the photograph's marks beside them do not resolve.
gaps.wanted: A higher resolution photograph of the front.

eth.description: the two 10/100/1000 Ethernet jacks, printed ETH 1 (upper) and 2 (lower)

attrs.redundancy-note: Digi Connect EZ 16/32 product page: "Product supports redundant replaceable power supplies". Its FAQ: "optional dual AC or dual DC power supplies". Neither states a form or whether the pair shares the load or one stands by, so 1+1 is read as one supply with one spare and the sharing is not stated.

psus.description: the two power supply bays, PSU1 on the right of the rear and PSU2 on the left

serial-lower.description: the lower row of sixteen RJ45 10-pin serial ports, printed 1 to 16 under it

serial-upper.description: the upper row of sixteen RJ45 10-pin serial ports, printed 17 to 32 over it

sfp-plus.description: the two SFP+ cages, printed SFP+ 1 (upper) and 2 (lower)

status-leds.description: the system lamps, Fan1, Fan2, Sys Fan, PSU1, PSU2, User, WWAN Signal and WWAN Service

usb.description: the two USB 3.1 Gen 1 Type A ports

name: connect-ez-32

bottom-layout.note: From the model: two square holes 10.0 across, six slots 5.6 x 2.8, eight round holes 4.0 across and twelve 5.5 across. The model does not say what they are for. Bottom view x is mirrored.

chassis.note: 444.0 x 44.0 x 255.0 from the body solid of the dimension model, the same in the EZ 16 and the EZ 32 files. The product page prints "25.5 cm x 44.5 cm x 4.445 cm (10.04 in x 17.5 in x 1.75 in)" labelled L x W x H, which agrees with the solid to 0.5 mm on every axis (255 mm depth, 444.5 mm width, 44.45 mm height in the nominal inches). The EZ 16 model's overall box is wider and deeper (476 x 269 mm) because it adds the rack ears (16 mm each side) and the thumbscrews and antenna jacks that stand 12 mm past the rear; those are drawn as parts and ears.

colour.note: The front and rear are black, the jacks have bright metal shields, the ears are black and the USB tongues are blue. Taken from the front and rear photographs.

ears.note: The product page says the unit "ships with attachable 19-inch rack ears". The model draws a bracket 16.0 wide, 43.5 high and 32.5 deep on each side, flush with the front face (its front plate in the plane of the face), with three slotted holes in the front plate (the photographs show them). No document states a position other than flush. No rail or mounting kit is listed on the product page.

front-layout.note: From the model: the console jack 15.9 wide centred at 34.0; the micro-SD socket 16.1 wide at 6.95; two USB Type A at 55.2 and 72.2 (centres, standing portrait); two SFP+ cages stacked at 89.1; two RJ45 jacks stacked at 112.6; two rows of four blocks of four serial jacks, each jack 16.0 wide on a 16.0 pitch, the blocks 70.0 apart from 130.3, the lower row at the EZ 16 model's y and the upper row stacked directly above it, which the EZ 16 model cannot show: the photograph puts its top edge about 3 mm lower than that, so its y is estimated; three columns of lamp light pipes at 410.5, 420.5 and 430.5. Whether the Ethernet jacks stack as drawn (14.6 each) is the model's.

gate-1.note: The EZ 32 front photograph is 800 px wide for the 476 mm of the face with its ears (1.53 px/mm across); every x on the front is the EZ 16 model's, which the photograph corroborates to about 2 mm (the console jack, the stacked jacks, the first and last serial jacks and the lamp cluster all fall within that). The model is orthographic, so this device is not measured off a photograph where the model has the feature; the photograph is a check and the source of the lamps, legends and colours. y is the model's height measured from the top (44.0 less its y).

lamp-layout.note: The three light-pipe columns are the model's; which lamp is in which is read off the front photograph: Fan1, Fan2 and Sys Fan in the first, PSU1, PSU2 and User in the second, WWAN Signal and WWAN Service in the third with a blue legend badge each. Good to about 1 mm.

lamps.note: The product page lists the system lamps "Power 1, Power 2, Fan 1, Fan 2, Sys Fan, User, WWAN Signal, WWAN Service" and per port "Ethernet, Serial, Console, USB". It says nothing of what a colour or a blink means, so the lamps carry on and off only.

ports.note: "SERIAL PORTS (RJ45 10-pin)": 32, RS-232 on the A models and RS-232/422/485 software selectable on the C (MEI) models; "CONSOLE (RJ45 10-pin)" RS-232; two 10/100/1000 Ethernet; two 10 Gb capable SFP+ sockets; two USB 3.1 Gen 1 Type A; a micro-SD socket that takes SD, SDHC and SDXC. The sockets are placed as parts with the mate each has in the library.

power.note: "AC: Single or dual AC input (C13 connector)"; "100 - 240 VAC, ~50 - 60 Hz, 2.4 A max for each power supply"; "DC: Dual DC power with EZ-AD00/EZ-CD00 models, with supplied Phoenix connectors"; "48 VDC, 2.9 A max for each power supply". Both are replaceable ("Product supports redundant replaceable power supplies"). No figure of power consumed by the unit is stated.

rear-layout.note: From the model, mirrored (a rear view reads left to right as the model's x runs right to left): the second power supply bay 95.0 x 41.5 at 4.5, the CORE module plate 133.2 x 22.8 at 99.5 (the model's plate is 136.5 wide and overlaps the supply's bay by 3.3 mm, so it is cut to the bay), the earth stud at 112 and 11 down, the system fan 54.7 x 41.8 at 289.8 (the model's is 58.1 and overlaps the first supply's bay by 3.4 mm) and the first supply 95.0 x 41.5 at 344.5. The antenna jacks, the reset pinhole, the warning legend and the earth symbol are read off the rear photograph (1.64 px/mm across, stretched about 1.2 times down) and are photo-measured.

side-layout.note: From the model, the wall's own holes. The left wall has a block of 13 x 9 square holes 2.0 across on a 3.0 pitch behind the front, and the right wall has the first two rows of the same block and a window 38.0 x 15.5 under it. Each wall has three round holes 3.0 across for the ear screws and the lid has two 5.9 holes per side and three 5.6 holes along its rear edge. Left view x = 0 is the rear and right view x = 0 is the front. On the top and the bottom view y = 0 is the rear and the bottom view mirrors left and right.

skus.note: The page lists six SKUs of this size: EZ32-A100-GLB (RS-232, global power cords), EZ32-A200-GLB (dual AC), EZ32-AD00 (dual DC), EZ32-C100-GLB (RS-232/422/485), EZ32-C200-GLB (dual AC) and EZ32-CD00 (dual DC). The photographs show one supply fitted and one bay covered, so the single AC build is the one pictured; the dual AC and dual DC builds are not pictured.

sources.note: Digi Connect EZ 16/32 product page (digi.com, read 2026-11-05): ports, power, dimensions, lamps, part numbers and accessories. Digi Connect EZ 16 and Connect EZ 32 dimension models ("footprint" STEP files EZ16-A000 and EZ32-A000, SolidWorks 2022, 2024-03-22): the EZ 32 file holds the same body solid as the EZ 16 file and its other solids are not placed in the body, so every position and size below marked drawing is the EZ 16 file's. The Connect EZ 32 front photograph and the shared rear photograph (800 px wide each): colours, legends, lamps and the counts the models do not name; the EZ 32 front photograph shows the same x for the console jack, the stacked jacks, the four serial blocks and the lamp cluster as the EZ 16 front photograph, to about 2 px. Digi's cable guide for PortServer TS, Digi One and Connect products: the pin counts of its cables. No data sheet or user guide is held; both are behind a form on the maker's site.

vent-row.note: A row of round perforations runs along the top of the front, 4.15 mm apart and about 2.8 mm across, from 79 to 431 mm; read off the front photograph and not in the model. It is drawn as the photograph shows it, with 85 holes. Good to about 1 mm.
